fixes.explanation: Not this one, friend. The text says the city was for a man who killed his neighbor "…unintentionally without prior malice." (Deuteronomy 4:42). Planning something for weeks is the opposite of unintentional. That's not the man the verse describes.

Good guess, friend, since a man running sure has a lot on his mind. But the verse says he flees "To save one’s own life…" (Deuteronomy 4:42). The word is life, not home. The text doesn't say where he was when he started running, and it doesn't say what happens to the house.

That's right, baker. Bezer belongs to the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead to the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan to the Manassites (Deuteronomy 4:43). Three cities, three tribes, one each. I'd say that's a pretty tidy list.

Nope, friend. The verse never mentions a king of Moab here. Each city belongs to a tribe: Bezer to the Reubenites, Ramoth to the Gadites, Golan to the Manassites (Deuteronomy 4:43). Moses is naming cities that belong to Israel's own tribes.
